informal_check.family_premises: For fixed n>=2, use the source row construction on a countably infinite pair universe. Every Li has an infinite private full row plus finitely many earlier row-prefixes, so languages are infinite and distinct. Any nonempty earlier subfamily intersection with Li is determined by its earliest index; the maximal finite one gives m_i=G(n,i)=sum(1<=j<i)n^j. The source explicitly sets m_1=0. Tail intersection has size G(n,i+1).
informal_check.stream_and_count: Each block-boundary prefix is distinct and is contained in the target selected at a stopping branch; enumerating the remainder gives an injective target stream. Its unseen point in L_j lies outside every later language, since their common finite prefix has been exhausted. If the late-error branch is avoided, boundaries 2,...,i_star count i_star-1 errors. The proof introduction's i_star-2 can be aligned textually but does not fix Big-O.
informal_check.constant_factor: For i>=2, T_i=G(n,i)+n^i+1=n*G(n,i)+n+1, since G(n,i+1)=n*G(n,i)+n. Because G(n,i)>=n, T_i<=(n+2)G(n,i)<=(n+2)max{i,m_i}. For i=1, T_1=n+1<=(n+2)max{1,0}. Thus every allegedly late boundary is itself O(max{i,m_i}) with an allowed class-dependent constant. For i growing, T_i/m_i tends to n, not infinity.
informal_check.quantifiers: The source selects one class before quantifying over algorithms, and its Big-O constant may depend on that class and algorithm. Choosing n after that constant changes the class and cannot establish the original quantifier order. No existence of a counteralgorithm or refutation of the headline theorem is concluded.
